body.p: Claims 1-19 are pending. Claims 9-19 are withdrawn. Claims 1-8 are rejected.
Applicant has amended claims 1 and 3-8. Claim 2 is cancelled without prejudice or disclaimer.
Claims 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8 are objected to due to informalities. Applicant has amended the claims to address these informalities. Withdrawal of the objections are respectfully requested.

Claims 2-8 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as being indefinite. Applicant has amended the dependent claims to clarify that the payload, payload handle and aircraft are not part of the claim. The claims are directed to the payload attachment device which is configured to attach to the aircraft and the payload. Withdrawal of the rejections are respectfully requested.
Claims 1 and 8 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) as being anticipated by Stevens (US 2868580).
Applicant's claim 1 includes features which neither disclosed nor suggested by the applied art, namely:

... a disconnectable electrical communication connection with a first end connecting at the payload attachment device and a second end configured for connecting to the payload handle when the payload handle is restrained.

Claim 1 has been amended to incorporate a modified version of the subject matter from claim 2, specifically adding "a disconnectable electrical communication connection with a first end connecting at the payload attachment device and a second end configured for connecting to the payload handle when the payload handle is restrained." In one example, the disconnectable electrical communication connection is shown as electrical contacts 270 and 350 in FIGs. 9A and 9B and described in paragraphs [0066]. In another example, the disconnectable electrical communication connection is shown as cable 320 in FIGs. 8A and 8B and described in paragraphs [0047], [0060] and [0063] of the specification. In either case, the disconnectable electrical communication connection provides a mechanism for electrically connecting the payload attachment device to the payload. This is beneficial for power and data transfer between the payload attachment device and the payload
In contrast, Stevens discloses a mechanical latching mechanism but is silent regarding
any electrical communication connection that is configured to connect the attachment device and the payload. Thus, claim 1 is patentable over Stevens.
Dependent claim 8 includes all the features of claim 1 from which it depends. Thus, claim 8 is also patentable over Stevens.

Claim 5 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as being unpatentable over Stevens in view of Duval et al. (US 2019/0308750). Duval discloses an electrical switching device for actuating a payload attachment device but is silent regarding any electrical communication connection that is configured to connect the attachment device and the payload. Thus, Duval does not make up for the deficiencies of Stevens.
Dependent claim 5 includes all the features of claim 1 from which it depends. Thus, claim 5 is also patentable over the combination of Stevens and Duval.

Dependent claims 3, 4, 6 and 7 are not rejected based on prior art. These claims include all the features of claim 1 from which they depend. Thus, these claims are also patentable over the applied art.
In view of the foregoing, it is respectfully submitted that this application is in condition for allowance. Favorable reconsideration and prompt allowance of the application are earnestly solicited.

If the Examiner has any questions or believes that any outstanding issues may be resolved with minor amendments or a phone discussion, the Examiner is invited to contact the Applicant's representative, William L. Bartow, at (215) 656-2458 or william.bartow(aus.dlapiper.com.
